substituent_description: A bicyclic system consisting of a fused 6-membered and 5-membered ring. The 6-membered ring contains a nitrogen atom shared with the 5-membered ring, a ketone at C2, an NH-COOBn group at C3, and a phenyl group at C4. The 5-membered ring has a COOMe group at C1 (hashed wedge) and an alkyl chain with a guanidine-like moiety substituted with two Boc groups at C2 (solid wedge). The bridgehead carbon between the two rings is substituted with a hydrogen atom (solid wedge).

A fused bicyclic system (diazadecalin-type) with an N atom at a bridgehead. A wedge bond attaches an 'MeOOC' group to the left six-membered ring. Another wedge bond at the bridgehead C attaches an 'H' atom. A double bond to 'O' is on the right six-membered ring, adjacent to an 'NH' group.

A fused 1,3-dithiole-benzene system. The dithiole ring is substituted with an exocyclic double bond leading to a carbon bearing an isocyano group and a benzoyl group. The benzene ring has a methyl group and two identical extended ester chains with O-(CH2)4-O-C(=O)-CH(CH3)-Et groups.
A benzothiazole fused ring system with a butyl (Bu) group at the 2-position and a methoxy (OMe) group at the 6-position.
A fused thiophene-pyrazole bicycle is substituted on the pyrazole nitrogen with a 3,4-dimethylphenyl group. The adjacent pyrazole carbon has an amide group linking to a 4-isopropoxyphenyl ring.

A tricyclic system containing a tetrahydropyran-like ring fused to a cyclopentenone and a pyrrolidine ring. The central six-membered oxygen-containing ring has a methyl group, an Ac group, and a Bn group. The five-membered ketone ring is fused adjacent to the oxygen ring. The nitrogen atom in the five-membered nitrogen ring is substituted with a Ts group.

A molecule consisting of a dipeptide-like backbone. The left part is an isobutyl derivative (iPr-CH2-CH(NHBoc)-C(=O)-), connected via an amide bond to a tryptophan derivative esterified with a benzyl group (NH-CH(COOBn)-CH2-indole). The indole ring is formed by fused 5- and 6-membered rings with alternating double bonds.

A complex molecule with a central piperidine ring substituted with a hydroxy group and a methylene group linking to a 3H-pyrrolo[2,3-d]pyrimidin-4(5H)-one derivative. The piperidine nitrogen is linked via a carbonyl to another piperidine ring which is substituted with a phenyl group and N-Boc protected. The pyrrolopyrimidine system is N-substituted with a benzo[d][1,3]dioxole group.

A phthalimide group is connected via its nitrogen atom to an ethylene chain, which links to a tertiary amide carbonyl. The amide nitrogen is substituted with a methyl group (Me) and a methylene group. The methylene group is attached via a hashed bond to the 3-position of a 4-ethyl-3,4-dihydro-2H-1,4-benzoxazine ring system.
A quinazoline core is substituted at position 7 with a methoxy group, at position 4 with a dimethylamino group, and at position 2 with an amino group that connects to a peracetylated pyranose ring.
